sources: SOURCE A: docs/GATE-2-CHECKLIST.md, the canonical GATE-2 specification
SOURCE B: docs/MILESTONE-VALIDATION.md, the milestone requirements of the audit
SOURCE C: LESSON-PREFLIGHT.json, the lessons the engineering memory imposes

requirements.description: A canonical, machine-readable requirement specification exists for this Gate and the registry mirrors it row for row.
The closed mandatory gate registry carries every executable gate this Gate introduces.
Every test suite this Gate introduces is declared canonically, is counted by the count derivation and is resolvable as evidence.
The internal Red Team battery of this Gate is executable, scoped to the Agent Runtime, and records a null-mutation control.
The reservation of the agent definition directory is consumed by the Gate that owns it, and the scope registry keeps constraining every path still owned by a later Gate.
One documented command verifies this Gate, adds the stages it introduces and keeps a targeted mode that does not restart the stack.
The agent runtime is a provider-neutral library with its own contracts, and the boundary decision is recorded rather than implied.
The runtime declares the persistence, model and clock ports it needs and imports no web application module, so the dependency points inward.
The runtime reaches a model only through the Model Gateway contract: no provider adapter, no provider client, no provider address and no credential exists inside it.
The runtime owns no retry policy, circuit breaker, fallback chain or provider selection of its own; those belong to the gateway.
No later-Gate capability — tool execution, sandboxing, retrieval, experience storage, quality scoring or training — is implemented, simulated or faked here.
The persistence layer is a shared package the API and the worker both depend on, so one authoritative schema definition serves both processes.
The agent definition directory stops declaring itself reserved and describes what this Gate delivered.
This Gate adds its schema through a new migration and edits no migration that has already been applied.
The existing task, run, agent and agent-run entities are evolved rather than duplicated; no parallel table is created for a capability an existing table already carries.
A database created from nothing reaches the head revision by running every migration in order.
A database at the Gate 1 revision upgrades to this Gate's head without losing the rows it already holds.
The run state vocabulary the database accepts is derived from one authoritative definition rather than written twice.
The run event log is append-only: it carries a creation time, no update time, and no code path rewrites a stored event.
A tool request and its result are separate persisted rows, and a request can carry at most one result.
Agent and team profiles are persisted with their version, and a row an operator has customised is not overwritten by a later bootstrap.
An agent run names the model calls that served it, and aggregate usage is derived from them rather than counted a second time.
The task content the workflow needs to continue is persisted, and the difference from the gateway's metadata-only record is documented rather than implied.
The run lifecycle is an explicit state machine over exactly the declared states, and no state exists that the contract does not name.
A transition happens only when the transition table allows it.
An impossible transition is refused with a typed error rather than silently applied.
A terminal state is terminal: no transition leaves `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED` or `CANCELLED`.
Re-running a task creates a new run; a terminal run is never resumed in place.
Every accepted state change records an event, so the history explains the state.
The state machine is one definition, used by the API, the workflow and the store alike.
The event vocabulary covers run creation and start, agent start and completion, model call start and completion, tool request and tool result, and the three terminal outcomes.
Events of one run carry a monotonic sequence number assigned by the store, so their order is deterministic.
A recorded event is never rewritten; a correction is a new event.
A retried append does not create a second event for the same occurrence.
An event payload carries a short verifiable summary and never a model's private reasoning or a raw prompt.
An event payload larger than the configured bound is refused rather than persisted.
An agent profile is a versioned contract carrying identity, role, description, prompt template, default route, turn limit, permitted actions and an enabled flag.
The builtin profiles are exactly the four this Gate needs to prove the runtime, and no profile exists for a capability the Gate does not exercise.
Profiles are loaded from the repository, enumerable through the runtime, and validated when they are loaded.
Loading the builtin profiles is idempotent: running it twice changes nothing the second time.
Prompt templates are versioned files under the agent definition directory, not strings concatenated across the code.
An agent run records the profile version and the prompt template hash that produced it, so its behaviour can be reproduced.
Prompt assembly keeps runtime instructions, role instructions, task content and tool results in separate labelled channels.
The user's task is carried in the user channel and is never concatenated into the system instructions.
Every executed step records run, task, agent, agent run, timestamps, model call identity, provider, model, template version and result status — and no private reasoning.
A profile declares the actions it may request, and a tool request outside that set is refused instead of persisted.
A team profile is a versioned, ordered list of stages, each naming an agent profile, its input mapping and the name of its output.
Two builtin teams exist: one single-agent and one two-stage planner and reviewer.
Team composition is configuration. Nothing in this Gate invents a team, and no model decides which agents run.
Stages execute in the order the profile declares, and each stage's output becomes explicit, named context for the next.
A previous stage's output reaches the next stage as a labelled artifact and never as an instruction.
A team run produces one agent run per stage, in order, with separate outputs.
A turn produces exactly one of a final answer, a message or a tool request.
The envelope carries an explicit version and is documented, so a consumer can detect an incompatible change instead of discovering one.
The parser is strict: an output that does not conform is rejected rather than partially accepted.
Native structured output is requested only from a model whose capability is known; otherwise the envelope is validated JSON text produced by the same contract.
No capability is asserted on a model's behalf to make a turn work.
At most one repair attempt follows an invalid turn, and it happens through the Model Gateway like any other call.
A repair call counts against the run's budget and is recorded as a repair rather than hidden.
A second invalid output ends the run with a normalised invalid-output error rather than looping.
Every inference this Gate performs travels through the Model Gateway client port and through nothing else.
A run may carry a route alias or an explicit model, and the gateway decides whether it can be served.
A run that names neither uses the configured default, and the runtime never picks a provider itself.
Every model call is attributed to the agent run that caused it.
A definitive gateway failure ends the run with a normalised error; the run never stays `RUNNING` for ever.
The runtime does not repeat a whole model call the gateway has already exhausted its own retries on.
Cost the gateway does not know is reported as unknown and never as zero.
A request the model's context cannot hold produces an explicit error rather than a silent truncation of the task.
A tool request is a persisted contract carrying identity, run, agent, name, arguments, creation time and a status from the declared vocabulary.
A tool result is a contract carrying the request it answers, a status, an output, an error and metadata.
A tool request turn persists the request, records the event and moves the run to `WAITING_FOR_TOOL`.
A paused run performs no further model call until a result arrives.
A tool name is data. Nothing in this Gate interprets it as a command, a path or an executable.
A matching tool result is persisted, recorded as an event and resumes the run.
The same tool result delivered twice resolves the request once and resumes the run once.
A tool result naming another run or an unknown request is refused.
A tool result that arrives after the run reached a terminal state is refused.
Waiting for a tool has its own configurable timeout, separate from the run deadline, and reaching it ends the run explicitly.

An automated control proves the runtime boundary contains no process, shell, filesystem-mutating or version-control execution path, and the control is a property of the boundary rather than of one file.
The division of labour with the next Gate is documented: this Gate persists and pauses, the next one executes.
Every run carries a maximum turn count, a maximum model-call count and a wall-clock deadline.
A token budget is enforced when the provider reports usage and recorded as unenforceable when it does not, rather than invented.
A budget that is zero, negative or absurd is refused when the run is validated.
Reaching any budget ends the run with a normalised budget error.
No model call happens after a budget is exhausted.
Every call to the gateway counts against the model-call budget, including a repair.
A run cannot execute an unbounded number of turns, and a run that outlives its deadline is ended rather than left running.
A run can be cancelled through the API while it is executing.
Cancellation reaches the durable workflow and stops it rather than only marking a row.
A cancelled run is terminal and records the cancellation event.
A run waiting for a tool can be cancelled, and a tool result that arrives afterwards is refused.
No model call happens after a run is cancelled.
Temporal is the durable execution engine, and no second scheduler or background orchestration loop competes with it.
Workflow code stays deterministic: every external effect — model call, persistence, notification — happens in an activity.
A worker restart while a run waits for a tool preserves the run, and the run resumes and completes when the result arrives.
An API restart does not lose a run in progress: the state lives in the store and in the workflow, never in process memory.
The workflow receives a frozen plan, so editing a profile while a run executes cannot change what that run is doing.
A versioned API creates a run, reads it, lists runs, streams its events, cancels it and accepts a tool result.
Creation answers immediately with the run identifier, its state and its creation time, without holding the request open for the run.
Creation accepts no provider credential and no provider address.
A run's status carries its state, current stage, timestamps, budget consumption, final result when there is one and error summary when there is one.
A failed run answers with an error type, a safe message, the stage that failed and the correlation identifier, and never with a traceback.
Run events are readable as a page and as a live stream.
A consumer that reconnects with a cursor receives exactly the events that follow it.
Reconnecting or retrying a read creates no new event.
The available agent profiles and team profiles are enumerable through the API.
Task input size is bounded by configuration and an oversized task is refused rather than stored.
A creation request repeated with the same idempotency key returns the run the first one created.
A creation request with a different key creates a different run.
Two runs execute at the same time without sharing state, context or events.
One task may carry two independent runs with separate results and separate events.
Identifiers use the strategy the repository already defines rather than a second format.
The runtime publishes the declared instruments for runs, turns, failures, waiting runs, budget exhaustions and cancellations.
No metric label carries a task, a prompt, a response or tool arguments, and every label is low cardinality.
Structured logs carry correlation, task, run, agent, agent run, stage, event type, model call and status when those exist.
No log record carries the whole task by default, and a secret nested inside a payload is redacted.
An operational page creates a run from a written task, a chosen team and an optional route or model.
The page follows the run's state and its events as they happen.
The page shows the final result of a successful run and the safe failure summary of a failed one.
The page can cancel a run that is executing.
A run waiting for a tool is shown as waiting, with the tool name and the pending status, and the page offers nothing that would execute it.
Model output is rendered as text, never as trusted markup.
No provider credential reaches the runtime, the store, a log record, a metric or the browser.
Tool arguments, agent output and tool results are bounded by configuration, and an oversized payload is refused.
Nothing this Gate persists becomes training data: rights default to denial and no run, event or result is marked otherwise.
The runtime asks for no private reasoning and stores none; what it keeps are short verifiable summaries.
A single-agent run executes live, through the Model Gateway, against the configured provider, and succeeds.
requirements.notes: Live single-agent run 01a0ca98-1a8d-7000-b79e-2cd9c93575d8 reached SUCCEEDED through the Model Gateway with every single.* check of scripts/iacode/agent_runtime_smoke.py passing (cmd-0006); the gateway's own live smoke passed every check against the same model (cmd-0005). Executed against openai:gpt-4o-mini, the provider and model the operator configured at closure after DevWorld's quota was exhausted; the decision is recorded in DECISIONS.md. The model was named explicitly and never substituted.

requirements.description: A planner and reviewer run executes live, in order, with separate outputs and the reviewer receiving the planner's output.
requirements.notes: Live planner-reviewer run 01a0ca98-22b0-7000-b413-63a35603e325 reached SUCCEEDED with two agent runs, plan then review, separate outputs and the reviewer reading the plan (cmd-0006). The first live attempts of the closure exposed G2-F-009 and G2-F-010; they are kept, as records made against the sealed GATE-2-CP-0001, in DECISIONS.md. Executed against openai:gpt-4o-mini, the provider and model the operator configured at closure after DevWorld's quota was exhausted; the decision is recorded in DECISIONS.md. The model was named explicitly and never substituted.

requirements.description: The live check uses an explicitly configured model and fails clearly when that model is not in the catalog, rather than substituting one.
The live check reports `BLOCKED` rather than `FAIL` when the local configuration carries no credential, and names the variable that is missing.
The live evidence records model provenance — provider, model, endpoint, model call identity — and no prompt or completion.
requirements.notes: The persisted MODEL_CALL_COMPLETED event of the live single-agent run records provider openai, model gpt-4o-mini, endpoint openai-chat-completions and model call 01a0ca98-204a-7000-90a0-de00c2388385, and carries no prompt, completion, content or messages field (cmd-0007); single.no_content_in_events and single.model_provenance passed live (cmd-0006). Executed against openai:gpt-4o-mini, the provider and model the operator configured at closure after DevWorld's quota was exhausted; the decision is recorded in DECISIONS.md. The model was named explicitly and never substituted.

requirements.description: The repository's one verification command covers this Gate, in its targeted and its full mode.
A runbook documents starting the runtime, creating a run, following it, cancelling it, tool requests and results, budgets, the live smoke and troubleshooting.
The architecture, development, version and entry documents describe what this Gate delivered rather than what was planned.
The structural decisions of this Gate are recorded as ADRs.
The Gate produces its retrospective from the canonical template.
The Gate closes at the project's own internal verdict and starts no part of the Gate that follows it.
Verify checkpoint validation must succeed from a detached checkout of the checkpoint tag
Verify a file inventory must be recomputed from the repository, never trusted as an assertion
Verify every operation attempt must be auditable, including a refusal decided before execution
Verify a checkpoint may never claim readiness while it also claims to be blocked
Verify a PASS requires evidence that can be executed or resolved, not a statement
Verify the repository must be self-contained; a specification may not live outside it
Verify independent validation cannot be declared by the run that did the work
Verify requirement completeness must be total and evidence-backed before handoff
Verify a red gate requires rework, never a waiver, and never a weakened check
Verify a recorded command must carry runtime, working directory, commit and purpose to be replayable
Verify a control over a checkpoint's own evidence must be scoped to the moment it matters
Verify sealed checkpoints and their tags are immutable, and tooling must keep validating them
Verify an installed capability must be detected by resolved path, not by a bare command lookup
requirements.notes: LSN-0013's only control is documentary, and this Gate detects no new capability: every executable it depends on is already recorded with its resolved path in docs/TOOL-CAPABILITIES.md.

requirements.description: Verify evidence must be recorded as it happens, not reconstructed at the end of a run
Verify every positive terminal status needs one shared promotion invariant
Verify a mandatory set must be closed by policy, never chosen by the caller
Verify a completeness denominator must come from a source the delivery does not own
Verify a structured reference must be resolved, not merely well typed
Verify a derived artifact must carry a fingerprint of the inputs that produced it
Verify evidence produced from a dirty tree needs immutable input identity
Verify sealed history needs an anchor outside the content it describes
Verify an authoritative count must be derived once, never maintained by hand twice
Verify a lesson must cite a source that actually records the finding it claims
Verify a control is finished only when its positive path has been executed, not only its refusals
Verify a generic guardrail derives repository state instead of naming today's checkpoint
Verify an adversarial battery without a null-mutation control proves nothing
Verify a lesson's prose may record a residual limit but may never contradict its status
Verify a configuration key that no code reads is a defect, not documentation
Verify a required protocol transition must never turn a mandatory gate red
Verify an empty applicable set is not a missing required set, and a control must tell them apart
Verify a control written while one Gate was the only Gate stops being a control when the next one starts
Verify a value bound in middleware is absent in the handlers that run outside it
Verify re-deriving what the framework already computed diverges from the framework
Verify captured subprocess output decoded or re-emitted with the platform codepage crashes the tool, not the work
Verify a gate that runs inside an image measures the image, not the source
Verify a shared control that names an identifier the repository derives stops being a control when that identifier moves
Verify two representations of one concept in one module disagree, and the safer one loses
Verify a test that writes to the operational database leaves production data behind
Verify a control that judges sealed history only runs once a successor anchors it
Verify an editing path that consumes a backslash escape leaves a control character, and the control it belonged to silently matches nothing
Verify a naming convention rewrites a CHECK constraint's name and leaves a UNIQUE constraint's alone
Verify a log line is not evidence that another process is ready
Verify a boundary scan must read the code rather than the prose, and must be shown to fire on a mutated module
Verify a counted test suite must declare its cases statically, because the denominator is read from the source
Verify a timeout that cancels the task it runs in leaves nothing able to record what happened
Verify a refusal that misnames the defect spends the only repair on the wrong correction
requirements.notes: The envelope parser is the validator whose refusal this Gate sends back as the instruction to correct. Absent or blank content keeps missing-content; a present value of the wrong type is content-not-a-string and the sentence names its JSON type. The live planner-reviewer run passed after the repair (cmd-0006), and the planner probe shows content as one string under the repaired contract (cmd-0008).

requirements.description: Verify a state and the event that explains it, written in two commits, are written event first
requirements.notes: Every terminal path of a run writes the terminal event before the terminal state: the engine's three outcomes, the workflow's deadline and unrecoverable paths, and the API path for a workflow that could not start. The live single-agent run recorded all seven events after the repair (cmd-0006).

requirements.description: Verify a metric read the instant after the call that moved it is read before the scrape that carries it
requirements.notes: Both checks of this Gate that read what Prometheus observes on its own cycle - the live gateway smoke and the Foundation smoke - wait up to three fifteen-second scrape intervals and ask only Prometheus, and a syntax-tree scan with a null control holds every Prometheus reader in the scripts to that. The gateway smoke failed on the race (cmd-0004) and passed after the repair (cmd-0005); the Foundation smoke failed on it after a fresh installation (cmd-0036, named by cmd-0038), G2-F-014, a GUARDRAIL_FAILURE against LSN-0049 resolved here. The full verification, fresh installation included, passed every stage after the repair (cmd-0067).

requirements.description: Verify a checkpoint sealed without naming its own tag cannot be validated from that tag
requirements.notes: This checkpoint is sealed with currentCommit naming its own canonical tag, which seal_checkpoint.py now enforces; the sealed GATE-2-CP-0001, which kept the symbolic HEAD, validates from its own tag under the derived binding. ADR-0023.
